I C.R.Y. 4u2 (Meadows)--- (Mmm… Lord know…) Born a day apart, storm twins in disguise, He Mississippi dust, I’m Carolina sky. Stafford paint drippin’, Mo-City in my stride, Two crooked reflections that the halo couldn’t hide. Marchin’ bands baptize, baptisms on beats, Cadillac confessions poured in plastic on the streets. We was holy in the grime, gospel crooked but it rhymed, Drumline ghosts still marchin’ in time. Mama said I cried in rhythm, heartbeat learned the snare, Father vanished early, but percussion kept me there. Pep wore Stafford stripes heavy, I wore Mo-City mud, Two boys with bent halos, armor built from blood. We fenced with our pride, hid scars under wraps, He flexed for applause, I countered with jabs. If lust ain’t split the bond, maybe kinship would grow, But temptation drew maps neither one could let go. PTSD hissin’, static loud in my head, I spoke my demons aloud, he said he bled. “I wasn’t alone”—echo calmed my night, But trust stayed locked, I still gripped tight. Sleepin’ light round men, ribs caged in steel, Even with his truth told, my locks stayed sealed. Rival sons of rhythm, faith cracked but true, Two marchin’ cadences in a drum-stained pew. Still ain’t clean, but I’m washed in the sound— (Washed in the sound!) Tried drownin’ in drank, grace pulled me out— (Grace pulled me out!) Friday horns ring bright when the field lights shine, Lord, it’s hard to leave when the beat feels divine. Still ain’t pure, but I prayed through the haze, Still marchin’ the drumline all my days. Still ain’t right, but the rhythm won’t fade, Cadence carved deep like a covenant made. We measured worth in chrome, in syrup floods, Bartered brotherhood’s gold for the glitter of mud. He cracked jokes sharp, I sparred for applause, Two kings uncrowned, heirs bound in flaws. Kids watched from bleachers, but we wore disguise, Grinnin’ in daylight, pain hid in eyes. He said “me too” when my PTSD roared, Two broken compasses pointin’ to the Lord. But mistrust weighed heavy, chains without key, Envy echoed in the brass melody. If we’d killed pride quicker, built bridges not bricks,, Grinnin’ in daylight, pain hid in eyes. He said “me too” when my PTSD roared, Two broken compasses pointin’ to the Lord. But mistrust weighed heavy, chains without key, Envy echoed in the brass melody. If we’d killed pride quicker, built bridges not bricks,10mo

Still Comin’ v3\[Theory\] \[mode | D Dorian blues\] \[tonal center | Dm\] \[meter | 4/4 shuffled swing\] \[tempo | 70 BPM trap-slow bounce\] \[chord color | blues-dominant with gospel IV-♭VII lifts\] \[Voice\] \[register | deep Southern baritone lead + male gospel tenor stack\] \[delivery | spoken-sung drawl, preacher runs, half-time Texas swag rap cameo\] \[expression | smoky → triumphant → hood-sanctified\] \[articulation | tight consonants, breath-audible verses, belt hooks, ad-lib overlaps at tails\] \[Style\] \[genre | Gospel-Trap Americana with Neo-Funk undertow\] \[era | ’70s tape warmth vs 2020s sub-low punch\] \[intent | weary lament → communal victory\] \[texture | upright bass, brushed kit, acoustic slide, Texas hats, pads\] \[aesthetic | porch-revival meets chopped-and-screwed\] \[focus | hook contrast, dynamic swells, cinematic lifts\] \[Timbre\] \[drum tone | woody snare rim, dirty 808, vinyl hats\] \[bass tone | resonant upright with tube \[Intro | 4 bars | Reverent Resolve + Low Heat; banjo pluck, deep 808s, gospel hums, switchblade-slide SFX\] " Muddy stream in my chest | still rising " (wind-sweep) " Delta name on steel | faith surviving " (banjo pick) " Cut the night | truth turns real " (switchblade-slide SFX) " Lord I’m listening | hold me still " (yes Lawd) \[Verse 1 | 12 bars | Wearied Lament; upright pocket, brushed kit, Leslie swirl\] " Born by that river | tent and thunder " (mmm) " Carved my mark | kept moving under " (vinyl hiss) " Long time coming | grit kept me " (Whoo) " Change keeps whispering | don’t leave me " (stomp-clap) " Doors swing wide | chrome remembering " (slide scrape) " Hearts play dice | faith’s surrendering " (press on) " I hold breath | count to seven " (hat shuffle) " Say her name | pray for heaven " (mmm) " Night gets loud | truth gets nearer " (organ swell) " I see myself | in broken mirror " (Whoo, testify!) " Drop the weight | keep on walking " (sub bloom) " Hope says stay | pain keeps talking " (still believin’) \[Chorus 1 | 8 bars | Triumphant Belt + Choir Halo; brass lifts, plate 1.2s\] " It’s been long | I kept running " (choir pad) " Storms hit hard | I’m still coming " (Whoo) " I know deep | change is coming " (brass stab) " Hold that line | dawn is humming " (yes Lawd) " River voice | says keep moving " (plate tail) " Dry these eyes | start improving " (press on) " Choir rise | hands go higher " (clap echo) " Change gonna come | stoke that fire " (still believin’) \[Verse 2 | 8 bars | Smoky Courage; banjo-organ answer lines\] " Gravel roads | taught patience slow " (banjo roll) " Sunday suits | learned where to go " (mmm) " Voices cracked | but kept their tune " (Leslie whirl) " Candles fought | a stubborn moon " (Whoo) " Back-porch vows | nails and twine " (rim click) " Blood and grace | held the line " (press on) " Bend that slide | mercy’s nearer " (slide moan) " Name the truth | make it clearer " (yes Lawd) \[Rap Break | 4 bars | Texas Bounce Swagger; double-time cameo\] " Fifth Ward prayers | wood-grain gripping " (UGK forever, ya heard!) " Screw in the sky | time still flipping " (vinyl chop) " Candy faith swing | pain lane switching " (mmm) " Green light hits | blessings start hitting " (808 check) \[Pre-Chorus | 8 bars | Communal Lift; quartet harmonies swell\] " It’s been long | keep on breathing " (choir) " Hands up high | hearts still beating " (room verb) " I know sure | dawn is nearer " (Whoo) " Say it loud | make it clearer " (still believin’) " Hold that note | don’t you break " (plate trail) " Faith ain’t cheap | truth ain’t fake " (yes Lawd) " Count it down | three then two " " Step together | we break through " (press on) \[Bridge | 8 bars | Key ↑ +2 | Exultant Testimony; full choir wave, sub-drop\] " Storms may rise | but not forever " (Whoo) " Fire survives | through any weather " (cinematic sweep) " He ain’t late | He’s on time " (yes Lawd) " Lift that weight | cross that line " (choir shout) " Feet keep time | drums keep calling " (mmm) " Saints and kin | catch me falling " (plate bloom) " River’s edge | turns to road " (press on) " Change arrives | heavy load " (sub bloom) \[Final Chorus | 12 bars | Victorious Belt + Chopped Repeat; half-speed tail, tape-stop\] " It’s been long | I kept running " (choir halo) " Storms hit hard | I’m still coming " (Whoo) " I know deep | change is coming " (brass stab) " Hold that line | dawn is humming " (yes Lawd) " Choir rise | hands go higher " (plate tail) " Change gonna come | stoke that fire " (still believin’) " A-a-a change | gon’ come now " (chopped) " Oh yes it will | slow down " (half-speed) " Hearts align | streets get brighter " (tape grit) " Bridges build | burdens lighter " (press on) " Lay it down | breathe together " (crowd swell) " Change arrives | right on schedule " (tape-stop prep) \[Outro | 4 bars | Spent Grace; banjo, stomp fade, whispered amen\] " Hmmm amen | keep me steady " (mmm) " Yes it will | always ready " (banjo pick) " River hush | holds my name " (yes Lawd) " Stomp two times | fade that flame "10mo

Slide-guitar cry with the 808 boom— UGK forever, we’ll be changin’ real soon! \[Pre-Chorus – Quartet Takes Over, Powerhouse Harmonies\] \*\*(Call)\*\* It’s been a long… (\*Long!\*) \*\*(Response – Choir)\*\* \*Long time comin’\* \*\*(Call)\*\* But I know… (\*I know!\*) \*\*(Response – Choir)\*\* \*A change gon’ come, oh yes, it will!\* \*\*(Tag – All)\*\* \*I still believe it!\* (\*Banjo riff, 808 sub-drop, cinematic sweep into next section\*) \[Bridge – Emotional Swell, Key Modulation ↑ E♭ m, Full Choir, Hands Raised\] Ohhh, but somehow I know (\*Know!\*) I keep pressin’ on (\*Press on!\*) \*\*Storms may rise, but my fire survives\*\* (\*Still burnin’!\*) ’Cause He don’t come late (\*Late!\*) He’s always on time (\*TIME!\*) (\*Cinematic sweep, slow 808 roll, stomps echo—tension building!\*) \[Final Chorus – Explosive, Full Gospel Energy, Half-Speed Chopped Repeat\] It’s been a long… (\*LONG!\*) A long time comin’ (\*Whoo!\*) But I know… (\*I KNOW!\*) A change gon’ come… (\*Oh yes, it will!\*) \*I still believe it!\* \*\[CHOPPED-AND-SCREWED REPEAT, half-speed, tape-stop tail\]\* A-a-a change… gon’ come… Oh-oh-oh yes… it will… (\*Banjo picks harder, spoons clicking, stomps relentless, 808s pulsing!\*) \[Outro – Choir Fades, Soft Banjo Pluck, Echoing Vocals\] (Hmmm… Lord…) (Yes, it will… yes, it will…) A change gon’ come… \*stomp-STOMP… fade…\*10mo

\[NSFW/Country-Trap Gospel Noir\] Getaway (Unhinged Scene One) by MoMoney Studios\[Theory\] \[mode | F minor with Phrygian lean\] \[tonal center | F\] \[harmonic behavior | sparse minor-root 808 tics, overdriven synth power chords, minimal chord movement\] \[meter | 4/4\] \[tempo | 142 BPM\] \[chord color | dark minor triads, lowered fifth distortion, sustained synth pads\] \[Voice\] \[register | mid to high baritone (DJ Mo/$ tag → hyped, energetic)\] \[delivery | aggressive shout-outs, chopped vocal stabs, rapid-fire ad-libs\] \[expression | gritty confidence, club-ready bravado, raw hype\] \[articulation | clipped consonants, stuttered pitch-shifts, abrupt tag drops\] \[Lyrics Narrative\] \[Intro (Lo-Fi Static, Faint Heartbeat)\] (Husband’s voice, weary, whispered) “I swear to God we were just friends…” (Lo-fi crackle + slow, heavy heartbeat beneath) “Suddenly… we were both lonely. You didn’t even notice… I’d started drinking again. ‘Cause I was lonely… and you just ignore… and hate all of my friends. You stopped looking at me. I became a ghost in our own home.” \[Verse 1 (Melancholic, Storytelling over distant bar ambience)\] “So I was at the bar… drinking alone.” (Glasses clinking faintly, murmurs, drink being poured) “She slid beside me… I thought I’d found a moment’s peace. A smile in the smoke, a kindness I hadn’t seen in weeks. But I swear to God, I didn’t mean to cross that line. A minute turned an hour… an hour felt like a sign. And her laughter, sharp like glass, cut through the fog.” \[Pre-Chorus (Suspenseful, Whispered Echoes + Subtle Static)\] “And your silence screams… ‘getaway’… cuts me to the bone. I felt it every time I walked through the door… cold like stone. Getaway… leave today… stay away…” (Echoing whisper, fading like a ghost) \[Verse 2 (Bar Scene, Her Discovery – Door Slam + Tense Heartbeat)\] (Sound: door slamming open) “And then she walked in… rage like a storm, eyes wild. How could you… why would… who is she? GETAWAY… LEAVE TODAY… STAY AWAY…” (Her voice distorted, overlapping, cracking) “Her breath like fire, her fists like thunder.” \[Chorus (Dramatic, Emotional Explosion with Vinyl Crackle)\] (Drums hit heavy, vinyl crackle underneath) “And I said… I’m sorry babe… I lost your trust today. I swear, I’ll do anything… please… just don’t turn away. I never meant for the ice between us… but I see it now.” \[Bridge (Minimal, Desperate Tone)\] (Husband’s voice, wavering, raw) “And she said… I’m sorry, I didn’t realize… I WASN’T THERE FOR YOU, AND WE BEEN TOGETHER TOO LONG… TO LET THIS MARRIAGE END. BUT FIRST… WE NEED TO WALK IN EACH OTHER'S SHOES… JUST SO YOU UNDERSTAND… so I need to meet her husband.” \[Chorus Reprise (Cold, Calculating – Subtle Static)\] (Static hum + tense heartbeat reprise) “And I asked WHY?” (Her voice, eerily calm, each word a knife) “I’m feeling lonely, I can’t ignore this. I refuse to let you two win. Imma be at her house… with her husband. After we spend the night in our bed.” \[Outro (Sparse, Vinyl Crackle, Looming Dread, Heartbeat Slowing)\] (Hollow, the room feels empty) “So while I get ready… I’m going to need you to… GETAWAY… LEAVE TODAY… STAY AWAY… until Sunday afternoon.” (Heartbeat slows, crackle deepens, fades into silence) \[Style\] \[genre | Dirty South × Neo-Crunk Revival × TikTok Club Banger\] \[era | 2025 streaming/TikTok resurgence\] \[intent | explosive high-energy trap fused with crunk grit\] \[texture | layered thunderous 808s, relentless rattling hi-hats, sub-heavy thumping bass, biting overdriven synth leads, chopped vocal FX, DJ scratches\] \[aesthetic | dark, aggressive, infectious, club-fueled\] \[focus | hyped drops with DJ tag, twerk-fueled sections, viral hook escalations\] \[Timbre\] \[808 tone | deep sub with gritty saturation\] \[hi-hat tone | metallic, rapid-fire open/closed hats\] \[synth lead | razor-sharp overdrive, resonant filter sweeps\] \[bass tone | sub-heavy punch with slight distortion\] \[vocal tone | in-your-face compression, pitch-bent chops, hyped hype shouts\] \[Performance\] \[execution | tight, hard-hitting drops; precise rhythmic sync; advanced scratching loops; pitch-bend flourishes\] \[gesture | rapid DJ Mo/$ tag drops, shout-outs, chopped vocal turns\] \[rhythm handling | quarter-note kick emphasis, syncopated hat rolls, triplet fills for twerk sections\] \[touch | aggressive gate delays, stutter edits on vocal chops, filter sweeps timed to each build-up and drop\] \[Outro Directive\] \[fade type | filtered low-pass sweep into sub-only decay\] \[outro vocal style | echoing tag repeat with pitch-down\]10mo

Country Booty Call (MoPlex Miix) (Remix)\[DJ Drop: Mo/$ DJ drops, crowd noise, filtered organ; Magz enters with cypher swagger, battle MC’s timing, ready to flip from spoken to melodic. Let every drop and shout have a trailer-pop wink.\] "Yo, it’s DJ Mo Money, Mo/$ on the decks!" (DJ drop) "Country girl meets Mo City trap beat kings—right here, right now!" (DJ drop) "We LYV at Mo Money Studios—twenty twenty-five, let’s go, bitches!" (DJ drop) \[Intro\] "Saddle dust on these city streets" (Crowd: Cheers, off-mic laughs) "Watch me shine, watch me eat" (Yeah) "Who said a girl can’t run this beat" (Real hot girl shit) "Saddle up, let's ride" (Giddy up) "This beat’s got the city on fire" (Yeehaw, let’s get it) "Ah-huh" (Let’s go) "Boots up!" (Now hush—let it ride) "Yeah, yeah, let's go" \[Verse 1: Use rapid-fire, internal rhymes and scientific multisyllabic phrasing; each line is bold but never loses the trailer pop melody. Lean into Eminem/Kendrick-style pocket flips, with a laugh or sneer where it fits.\] "Big buckle on my waist, neon on my name" (Whoop) "Boots so loud, they got cows feelin’ shame" (Laughter) "Mama said don’t chase those cowboy games" (Quick inhale before next bar) "But I turn that lasso into diamond chains" "He slide in my DMs talkin’ queen of the hay" "I ghost him quicker than I cash my pay" "Bass in the barn, that crowd on mute" "Boots on the porch, just me and my truth" "Country heart, city wit—can’t clone this blend" "I’m that wild-card girl, flexin’ 'til the end" \[Chorus: Hooks are melodic, anthem-ready, but cut through with battle-rap confidence and trailer-park swagger. Ad-libs should have a gospel or crowd chant bounce, with “white girl math” punchline attitude.\] "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Who’s got the boots to ball" (Crowd: "We do!") "Thick like syrup, I stick on the drawl" "Raise your cup if you heard this y’all" (Let’s go!) "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Heads turn, let ‘em fall in line" "Spin that bag, I don’t need his co-sign" "Wave your hats, let the spotlight shine" (Mis-timed clap, quick laugh left in) \[Verse 2: Drop a Boosie/Pimp C trill flex—confessional and punchy, weaving multis, trailer wisdom, and country references. Allow for micro-story and a joke or two.\] "Moonshine sippin’ out a Yeti with gold" (Off-mic whistle) "Grandpa’s truck, still ain’t been sold" "They wanna wife me for the farm and the land" "But I’m buyin’ out deeds, got my own brand" "Mama warned don’t trust his rodeo smile" "But I walked in the ring, made the judges wild" "Hat tip, crowd flip, I bend that scene" "Bass knock, boots drop, I’m the real country queen" (Voice cracks on "promo," keep it) "Farm girls mad, that’s free promo" "Catch me dancin’ in the city solo" \[Bridge: Acapella, half-spoken, Kendrick-style confession—channel the vulnerability of battle defeat and the bravado of comeback. Keep the phrasing loose, leave in the breaths, and let gospel hums echo in the background.\] "Heard girl, you can’t—since age thirteen" (Breath, near whisper) "Now I’m headline news in these boots money green" "Tried to box me in—no roof, no wall" "Country flex—watch me, no filter at all" "Phone blowin’ up, county boys in a trance" "But I’m just out here givin’ every girl a chance" (Shaky sigh, tape wobble) \[Chorus (Final): Anthem dialed to max, gospel choir behind, Magz throws in extra rhyme flips and closes with a battle-winner’s wink. Let crowd ad-libs run wild.\] "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Who’s got the boots to ball" (Let’s go) "From hayloft to high-rise, watch me run it all" "Thick as trouble, sweet as the county drawl" "Country booty call" (Crowd, wave them hats, let the barn lights fall) "I’m the headline, read it on the wall" (Late cheer, stray harmony on "call") "Boss talk, one glance—y’all know who to call" \[Outro: Band drops out, acapella with gospel melisma; Magz riffs, lets a laugh or voice crack land, closes with Mo/$ DJ drop. Let the last line hang, full of attitude and promise.\] "Kick dust, blow a kiss, tip the brim" (Boots up!) "Who’s the queen, say my name again" (Country girl signed out) "Bass fades, I wink, camera flash" "Roll out solo, let the rumors dash" "Now watch ‘em all try to copy the route" (Mo/$: "Magnolia Magz, Mo Money Studios, twenty twenty-five!")11mo

u2\[STYLE\] Genre Fusion: Southern Gothic, Trap, Gospel Narrative: A betrayed individual moves from silent, internal conflict to cold, calculated retribution. The tone is not one of rage, but of eerie calm and divine correction. Mood: Initially mournful and heavy, transitioning to a confident, almost transcendent menace. The final mood is one of stoic, unsettling justice. \[TIMBRE\] Primary Instruments: A solo, clean banjo (with a crisp attack), deep 808s, and a full gospel quartet for harmonic support. Accents: Sharp, percussive gospel hand claps, and subtle, ambient string swells. Textures: The overall track should have a lo-fi, vinyl-era texture. The banjo should be dry and intimate, while the gospel vocals should be doused in a long, dark plate reverb. \[PERFORMANCE\] Vocal Delivery: Starts with a quiet, almost spoken-word delivery that builds to a rhythmic, rapid-fire flow. The final verse should be delivered with an unsettling calmness. Vocal Persona: A narrator who is both a victim and a vengeful deity. The voice is steady, but every word carries the weight of a spiritual vow. Rhythmic Phrasing: The vocals ride the beat with a conversational, yet percussive flow, punctuated by strategic pauses.11mo

Can YOu Stand The Rain (Suno and Mo Remix) (Instrumental) (Remix)Under a neon haze just past the Mississippi line, the velvet-walled juke joint pulses with sweat, perfume, and a deep rattling bass. The crowd shifts as DJ MoMoney steps to the mic, voice chopped and filtered through static, declaring: 'Ayo! This one for the ladies! Boss chicks only! Drop it low, let’s GO!' As swirling synths and ambient pads rise behind him, chopped vocals echo into darkness while 808s creep in slow, setting the ritual in motion. A contralto vocalist, smoky and confident, steps into the first verse with calm intensity: 'You and me, we made a vow, for better or for worse. Can’t believe you let me down, but the truth, oh, how it hurts.' Her voice rides smooth R&B chords and gliding 808s, while crowd chants simmer just below the beat. She stays locked in the pocket, restrained but resolute, the groove breathing with hi-hats and subtle swing. As the pre-chorus swells with percussive claps and synth risers, she leans into the mic, her phrasing rhythmic and questioning: 'I see the storm clouds rollin’ in, but can we dance in the rain again?' Falsetto echoes curl behind her as tension lifts and the crowd leans forward. Then, the floor explodes with the first chorus—an anthem designed for sweat and sweat equity. A chant rises, group vocals commanding: 'Can you stand it? (Ayy!) Can you stand it? (Woo!) Drop that, shake that, bounce it, break that!' 808s slam. Synths pulse. The room moves as one body. Without pause, a bold female rapper takes the verse by storm, her flow fast and unrelenting: 'Body like a problem, boy, solve that quick! Stack real thick, got ‘em throwin’ them bricks! Drip stay cold, but the way I drop heat, hips don’t lie, make ‘em weak in the knees!' Then, switching speeds mid-line: 'Throw that back, put the money where ya mouth is, slow whine, then I hit ‘em with a bounce flip! Never been a rookie, all-star when I play, boss moves only, make ‘em rain all day!' Her voice rides over synth banjos and chopped trap hats, glitch accents snapping like gum and gunfire. Suddenly, the room spirals into a syrupy breakdown. DJ MoMoney’s voice slows and deepens: 'Sloooow it doooown.... Now bring it BACK!' Behind him, vocals are warped and reverb-drenched. A call and response ignites between the lead and crowd. 'Tell me, can you stand it?'—'Can you stand it?' they shout. 'Love’s like a storm, can you take it?'—'Can you take it?' And with a sonic slam, the beat returns, full throttle. The final chorus arrives like a wave cresting. Chant vocals rise again: 'Can you stand it? (Ayy!) Can you stand it? (Woo!) Drop that, shake that, bounce it, break that!' Club synths reach a peak, gospel pads flare, and the dancefloor becomes holy ground. Finally, the outro strips the sound down to 808 thumps and a lone voice in the mist. DJ MoMoney, raw and proud, calls out one last time: 'That’s how you do it! Queens only! If you ain’t bringin’ that energy, STAY HOME!' His voice fades into crowd ambience, chopped vocal echoes, and the hiss of tape running out. This track is a southern revival of trap gospel soul—where heartache dances, bass baptizes, and no one leaves unshaken."11mo

Charleston, South Carolina born. Raised between Columbia's Five-Points scene and weekends immersed in Athens, GA and Pigeon Forge juke joints. College years at University of Georgia, with heavy influence from Austin's 5th Street bars and Houston's Big Easy blues jams. Regular pilgrimages to D/FW on weekends. Influenced by Lynyrd Skynyrd, Hank Jr., DJ Screw, Danjah Ra (mddlfngz), Soul Train, Hee Haw, Top 40 radio, and Lawrence Welk. Learned stage craft from Luther and The Healers. Studies include Robert Johnson (guitar), Hans and Candy Dulfer (woodwinds). Prioritizes feel and phrasing over technical perfection.\[Narrative Summary\] Charleston, South Carolina born. Raised between Columbia's Five-Points scene and weekends immersed in Athens, GA and Pigeon Forge juke joints. College years at University of Georgia, with heavy influence from Austin's 5th Street bars and Houston's Big Easy blues jams. Regular pilgrimages to D/FW on weekends. Influenced by Lynyrd Skynyrd, Hank Jr., DJ Screw, Danjah Ra (mddlfngz), Soul Train, Hee Haw, Top 40 radio, and Lawrence Welk. Learned stage craft from Luther and The Healers. Studies include Robert Johnson (guitar), Hans and Candy Dulfer (woodwinds). Prioritizes feel and phrasing over technical perfection. \[Theory\] \[mode | minor blues with modal shifts\] \[tonal center | B♭\] \[harmonic behavior | minor vamp, gospel turnaround overlays, suspended tensions, drone pedal underlays\] \[meter | 4/4\] \[tempo | 76 BPM with variable swing\] \[chord color | minor 9s, diminished pulls, open-fifth drone under choruses\] \[Voice\] \[register | baritone male lead (low tenor edge), high falsetto pre-chorus, female gospel harmonies (alto + soprano)\] \[delivery | lead switches between spoken-word, confessional belt, and whispered descent; falsetto used for pre-chorus intensity; adlibs float above choruses\] \[expression | guttural grief, outlaw bravado, sensual grit, gospel pleading\] \[articulation | slurred phrasing, syncopated drops, gospel melisma on pre-chorus, clipped stabs in drill flow\] \[Intro (Gospel Quartet, A Cappella Harmony)\] (Ohhh… they say let go… but I can’t… I won’t…) (I touch shadows… but they don’t fade… no…) \[Verse 1 (Spoken Flow, Cold & Heavy)\] I don’t understand… how they expect me… to… Am I really… supposed to be able… to… Forget and forget? (I say it like that.) Because I’m never forgiving you. When the smell of that place… Puts me right to that moment… My body’s here, but my mind still frozen… Like a ghost that can’t move on… \[Pre-Chorus (Female Lead, Gospel Harmony)\] (Ohhh… tell me how… tell me why…) (Do I drown or survive…?) (They say time will heal my pain…) (But the scars still say your name…) \[Chorus (Gospel + 808s Drop)\] The roses I touch, Magical it must… be. They say of you, I think too much… see. \[Verse 2 (Drill Flow + Off-Grid Swing)\] Bipolar swings like a pendulum blade, Some days I shine, some days I fade. Some days I fight, some days I cave, Got scars on my soul that I can’t erase. Whiskey in my cup, demons in my chest, Prayin’ to a God that I second-guess. Tryna stay clean, but the past won’t rest, Every step I take, I feel possessed. \[Bridge (Slow Down, Gospel Harmonies)\] (Take my hand... lead me home...) (Break these chains... I can’t go alone...) (Tell me there’s more, tell me there’s light...) (Tell me my past won’t take my life...) \[Verse 3 (The Breaking Point)\] I see your face in the dark when I sleep, I hear your voice when the silence runs deep. They say "move on," they say "let it be," But how can I heal when it’s still in me? This ain't revenge—this is truth, this is proof, This is the rage that they bottled in youth. If they want silence, they won't get their way, I touch shadows, but I won’t fade away. \[Outro (Gospel A Cappella + 808s Fade)\] (Forget and forget… I say it like that…) (But I’m never forgiving you… never forgiving you…) (Gone… gone… gone…) \[Style\] \[genre | Experimental Outlaw Trill, R&B Blues Noir, Tribal Gothic Soul\] \[era | 2025 cinematic R&B x outlaw hip-hop hybrid\] \[intent | confessional trauma vs outlaw defiance:: sacred grief vs club defiance\] \[texture | extreme dynamic contrast, atmospheric sound design, hybrid soul-trap grit\] \[aesthetic | haunted gospel meets DJ set:: raw-to-polished contrast\] \[focus | vocal performance layering, gospel-to-drill rhythmic fusion, DJ drop integration\] \[Timbre\] \[guitar tone | bluesy ambient licks, filtered distortion on accents\] \[bass tone | evolving tuned 808s, sub boost during chorus drops\] \[drum tone | tribal trap kit with ethnic textures, layered syncopation\] \[keyboard tone | gospel organ swells, lo-fi synth pads, warped arp delays\] \[vocal tone | baritone dry-spoken vs wet falsetto layers:: distant female gospel wash\] \[Performance\] \[execution | alternating sections of restraint and explosion; falsetto layered under gospel hook\] \[gesture | DJ drop emphasis, delayed beat drops, vocal FX cuts\] \[rhythm handling | swung trap phrases with off-grid syncopation, gospel-call patterns\] \[touch | mic proximity breath details, lo-fi noise overlays, reversed vocal swells\] \[Outro Directive\] \[fade type | vocal decay over atmospheric gospel hum and sub-bass fade\] \[outro vocal style | slow whisper + falsetto ghost layers\] \[End\]11mo

Three Generations (Foxy's On Friday pt.2) (Remix)\[Intro: (Slow Ride 808s, Melancholy Synth Pad, Distorted Guitar Drone)\] (Weary Female Vocal - Spoken Word) "...neon... always neon... same damn dance... generations..." \[Verse 1: (Deep Southern Drawl Vocal, Conversational Rhythm, Subtle Hi-Hats)\] "Neon sign buzzes, a broken-wing fly, Another spilled beer, another forced smile, high. Tray heavy laden, feet swollen and sore, No 401k waiting, just closing the door." "Used to be diamonds, now just dusty glass, Reflecting back faces, that time lets surpass. These young girls they hustle, with eyes bright and bold, My story’s been told, growing weary and cold." \[Pre-Chorus 1: (Building Synth Melody, Rhythmic 808 Pulse, Hint of Fiddle)\] "Used to be music, used to be heat, Used to be rhythm, movin' these feet. Now just the echoes, in this tired old place, And memories hauntin', every line on my face." \[Chorus: (Melancholy Vocal Melody, Gospel-Infused Backing Vocals, Heavier 808s, Distorted Guitar Chords)\] "Three generations under neon light, Same stage, different dancers, in the fading night. Three generations, caught in the undertow, Where the dreams go to die, and the secrets grow." \[Verse 2: (Introspective Vocal, Slower Pace, Chopped & Screwed Vocal Echo on Key Words)\] "Foxy’s on Friday, bass drum in the chest, 6 10 traffic, put life to the test. Smell of cheap perfume, and sweat in the air, Felt like forever, but nobody stays there." "Silk robes and shadows, a dance in the haze, Caught in the moment, lost in those days. Grandma she warned me, with eyes full of rain, “Beauty’s a vapor, a fleeting, sweet pain.”" \[Pre-Chorus 2: (Heightened Synth Intensity, More Prominent Fiddle, Snare Drum Enters)\] "Grandpa he chuckled, with wisdom so deep, “New models keep comin’, while old dreams just sleep.” But we didn’t listen, to whispers so true, Thought we were different, thought we’d break through." \[Chorus: (More Powerful Vocals, Fuller Gospel Harmonies, Heavier Instrumentation)\] "Three generations under neon light, Same stage, different dancers, in the fading night. Three generations, caught in the undertow, Where the dreams go to die, and the secrets grow." \[Bridge: (Stripped Down to Acoustic Guitar and Vocal, Pedal Steel Atmosphere, Building Intensity)\] (Raw, Emotional Vocal) "Mirror shows wrinkles, where laughter lines played, Body worn down, by the choices we made. Each ache is a memory, a price we all pay, For chasing the spotlight, and losing our way." (Synth Pad and 808s Re-enter, Gospel Harmonies Swell) "See the new owner, slick hair and fake grin, Showing some girl, where the heartache begins. Another young sparrow, about to take flight, Into the darkness, of neon-soaked night." \[Breakdown: (Chopped & Screwed Instrumental Section - 808s, Synth Chops, Distorted Guitar Screams)\] (No Vocals - Instrumental Break - Emphasize Houston Trill and Despair) \[Verse 3: (Whispered, Heartbroken Vocal, Minimalist Beat Returns)\] "Walking out weary, head bowed to the floor, Thought I was finished, walking of those doors...." \[end\]11mo

\[IINDIE POP-Neo Soul \] Forget and Forget### \*\*\[Intro – Gospel Quartet, A Cappella Harmony\]\*\* \*(Ohhh… they say let go… but I can’t… I won’t…)\* \*(I touch shadows… but they don’t fade… no…)\* ### \*\*\[Verse 1 – Spoken Flow, Cold & Heavy\]\*\* I don’t understand… how they expect me… to… Am I really… supposed to be able… to… Forget and forget? (I say it like that.) Because I’m never forgiving you. When the smell of that place… Puts me right to that moment… My body’s here, but my mind still frozen… Like a ghost that can’t move on… ### \*\*\[Pre-Chorus – Female Lead, Gospel Harmony\]\*\* \*(Ohhh… tell me how… tell me why…)\* \*(Do I drown or survive…?)\* \*(They say time will heal my pain…)\* \*(But the scars still say your name…)\* ### \*\*\[Chorus – Gospel + 808s Drop\]\*\* The roses I touch, Magical it must… be. They say of you, I think too much… see. ### \*\*\[Verse 2 – Drill Flow + Off-Grid Swing\]\*\* Bipolar swings like a pendulum blade, Some days I shine, some days I fade. Some days I fight, some days I cave, Got scars on my soul that I can’t erase. Whiskey in my cup, demons in my chest, Prayin’ to a God that I second-guess. Tryna stay clean, but the past won’t rest, Every step I take, I feel possessed. ### \*\*\[Bridge – Slow Down, Gospel Harmonies\]\*\* \*(Take my hand... lead me home...)\* \*(Break these chains... I can’t go alone...)\* \*(Tell me there’s more, tell me there’s light...)\* \*(Tell me my past won’t take my life...)\* ### \*\*\[Verse 3 – The Breaking Point\]\*\* I see your face in the dark when I sleep, I hear your voice when the silence runs deep. They say "move on," they say "let it be," But how can I heal when it’s still in me? This ain't revenge—this is truth, this is proof, This is the rage that they bottled in youth. If they want silence, they won't get their way, I touch shadows, but I \*\*won’t\*\* fade away. ### \*\*\[Outro – Gospel A Cappella + 808s Fade\]\*\* \*(Forget and forget… I say it like that…)\* \*(But I’m never forgiving you… never forgiving you…)\* \*(Gone… gone… gone…)\*11mo

Granny's Porch Jam v2\[Theory\] \[mode | F major with Lydian flavor\] \[tonal center | F\] \[harmonic behavior | rich major chord vamps, gospel IV–V–I progressions, suspended second resolves\] \[meter | 4/4\] \[tempo | 68 BPM swung gospel pace\] \[chord color | lush seventh chords, extended harmonies, warm organ pad swells\] \[Voice\] \[register | lead: soulful alto → warm, inviting; choir: mixed SATB with warm blend\] \[delivery | lead: gentle drawl building to passionate calls; choir: tight harmonies with dynamic swells\] \[expression | heartfelt exhortation, reverent worship, communal uplift\] \[articulation | smooth legato on held notes, crisp consonants on call-and-response lines\] \[Intro (Slow Build, Soulful Harmonies)\] \*(Soft Rhodes keys, distant organ swells, deep bass humming, and a gentle brushed snare as the choir hums in harmony.)\* \[Lead:\] Ohhh, you gotta get ready now… (mmm-hmm) Ohhh, no man knows the day or the hour… \[Verse 1\] Get your house in order, oh do it today Get your house in order, oh do it right away For Jesus is coming, no man knows where or when Get your house in order, for He’s coming back again \[Chorus: Call and Response\] \*\*(Lead:)\*\* Get your house in order... \*(Choir echoes: In order!)\* \*\*(Lead:)\*\* Oh, don’t wait too late... \*(Choir echoes: Don’t wait!)\* For Jesus is coming... \*(Choir: Coming!)\* He's coming back again \*(Soft instrumental break – bluesy guitar and organ swells as the choir hums in harmony.)\* \[Verse 2\] There’s earthquakes, hurricanes, famines, and disease Can’t you hear the Lord is callin’? You better take heed... So many homeless, lost out in the cold But my God’s got mansions More precious than gold \[Chorus: Repeat\] Get your house in order, oh do it today Get your house in order, oh do it right away For Jesus is coming, no man knows where or when Get your house in order, for He’s coming back again \[Bridge: Soft Breakdown – Transition Begins\] \*(The music softens, Rhodes and bass pulsing gently, as the lead starts to testify.)\* \[Lead:\] Ohh, but there’s something, something about His name... \*(Choir hums in agreement, warm harmonies swelling.)\* \*(Rhodes swells, drums build lightly, leading into the next movement…)\* \[Transition – “Something About the Name Jesus”\] \*(Organ swells, deepening bass, light hi-hats as the choir takes the lead.)\* \[Chorus: Something About the Name Jesus\] Something about the name Jesus, Something about the name Jesus, It is the sweetest name I know... Oh, how I love the name Jesus, Oh, how I love the name Jesus, It is the sweetest name I know... \[Call and Response: Intensifying Worship\] \*(Lead with passion, choir responding powerfully.)\* \[Lead:\] Some say it’s like fire shut up in my bones… \[Choir:\] Fire in my bones! \[Lead:\] Oh, the Holy Ghost is moving, I can feel it strong… \[Choir:\] He won’t leave us alone! \*(Drums pick up slightly, adding energy to the moment.)\* \[Chorus Repeat: Full Power\] Something about the name Jesus, Something about the name Jesus, It is the sweetest name I know... \*(Music slows again, returning to the original theme.)\* \[Outro: Returning to "House in Order"\] \*(Soft Rhodes, deep bass, and light drum taps as the energy comes back down.)\* Get your house in order, oh do it today… Get your house in order, oh don’t delay… \*(Lead whispers, choir softly echoing: “For He’s coming… back… again…”)\*\*\*11mo

Boots Up, Shots Down (County Line Anthem) base (Remix)\[Style: Country-Trap Anthem with Honky-808 Bounce, Slide-Guitar Swag, Arena Crowdants, and Vinyl Lo-Fi Dust Vocalist & Performance Attributes Vocalist: Female Alto – Husky, Resonant,-Capable Timbre: Warm and gritty, with a whiskey-soaked edge; transitions effortlessly from an intimate whisper to a powerful arena belt.: D3E5 (chest dominant), with falset extending to F5 the. Delivery Style: Intro//Outro: Whisper-sung, breathy, and close-mic’d for intimacy. Verses: Relaxed with a Southern-twang swagger and rhythmic pacing. Chorus: Bold and full-bodied chest voice with emphasized hard consonants features crowd call-and-response chants. Bridge Belt: Builds dynamically from a whisper to a full belt with grit. Backing Vocals: Gang Shout Ensemble – Mixed male/female group (alto-tenor-baritone) Attributes: Energetic stadium chants slight det and a wide stereo spread. ightly synced post-drop, with a high-pass filter at 200Hz to maintain airy. Enhanced with layered clap and stomp effects in the chorus for a live anthem feel. Notable Techniques: \[Whispered Intro\] incorporating vinyl texture and cowbell ticks. \[Rap-Sing\] in the bridge section with rhythmic phrasing supported by a Rhodes chord bed. \[Falsetto Outro\] performed with breathy sustain and a tape roll-off EQ effect.\] \[DJ DROPS, TAGS, AND INTRO – Studio Room Noise, Crowd FX\] “Yo, it’s DJ Mo Money, Mo/$ on the decks!” “Country girl meets Mo City trap beat kings—right here, right now!” “We LIVE at Mo Money Studios—twenty twenty-five, let’s go, bitches!” (Crowd: Cheers, off-mic laughs, room noise) \[Intro, Whisper, Vinyl Crackle, Cowbell Tick\] "Psst—y’all hear them subs?" "Boots up… shots down… let’s ride!" \[Verse 1, Banjo Chops, Slide Flairs, Sparse Hats\] "Red dirt on my Louboutins, chrome snake buckle shine" "I pour sweet tea in my whiskey—double trouble every time" "Trunk knock harder than a back-road pothole" "I rev that Chevy heartbeat while the neon takes control" \[Pre-Chorus 1, Fiddle Stabs, 808 Build\] "Skirt hem frayed, but my game on ten" "They talk— we walk— then we spin again" \[Chorus 1, Beat Drop, Gang Shouts\] GANG: "Boots up, shots down!" LEAD: "Country queens wear the county line crown" GANG: "Boots up, shots down!" LEAD: "We turn dirt roads into Boom-Town sound" \[Verse 2, Slide Guitar Answers, Trap Hats Triplet\] "Pink camo phone case, snakeskin press-ons" "Snapback tilted, that rebel spirit strong" "City boys stare at my steel-toe strut" "I’m a two-step trouble with a homegrown gut" \[Testimony Rap-Sing, 808 Run, Rhodes Chords\] "Mama said, ‘Baby, raise hell but stay kind’" "So I tip big, talk slick, keep Jesus on the line" "From pew to pool-hall—we break the mold" "Country girl magic with a heart of gold" \[Pre-Chorus 2, Call/Response Fiddle Licks\] "Skirt hem frayed, but my game on ten" "They talk— we walk— then we spin again" \[Chorus 2, Chorus Repeat + Crowd Claps\] GANG: "Boots up, shots down!" LEAD: "County line ladies run this town" GANG: "Boots up, shots down!" LEAD: "We make cowboys drop their jaws to the ground" \[Bridge, Whisper-to-Belt, Reverse Pedal-Steel, VinylStop\] "Shhhh—hear that hush before the storm?" "Kick drum thunder, fire keepin’ us warm" (Beat drops back in w/ fiddle scream) \[Breakdown, Half-Time Trap, Banjo Fill, Crowd Chant Loop\] GANG LOOP: "Boots up—shots down—boots up—shots down" \[Guitar Solo, Tele Slide Over 808s\] \[Final Chorus x2, Full-Tilt, Double Harmony, Crowd Scream\] (Repeat Chorus lines, add octave-up harmony and ad-lib “Yee-yee!”) \[Outro, Whisper Falsetto, Fiddle Fade, Tape Click\] "Dust settles but our anthem won’t" "County line queens—forever they’ll quote" \[Studio Tail-Out, Friends Whoopin’, Cans Clank\] Engineer: “Print it—bar’s already callin’ for that one!”11mo

The Soul Sessions:: Through The Fog (Quartet) v4 (Remix)\[Intro – Spoken/Organ\] “Mmm… sometimes… you try to remember… but all you see… is fog. Lord have mercy…” (stomp) Lead: “Ooooh Lord, take me back through the fog.” (Ad-lib: “Through the fog… Amen!”) \[Verse 1\] We are born of sin, fight to win, without you I ain’t whole… got lost in the cold. Every night I pray to see your face; this fog got me reachin’ into empty space. (Ad-lib: “Reachin’ into empty space”) \[Chorus\] Through the fog I reach for you; time stole the colors and left me blue. Thirty-five years drownin’ in tears, but I fight to remember, fight through the fear. (Ad-lib: “Through the fog…”) \[Verse 2\] Wish that call never rang in the dead of night… wish I had more than echoes and pain. Oh Lord, this fog done stayed too long. (Ad-lib: “Stayed too long”) \[Bridge\] I close my eyes, try to pull you from the mist… it breaks me. I don’t wanna forget you, but remembering hurts… this fog ain’t mercy—it’s a curse. \[Chorus ×2\] Through the fog I reach for you; smoke and truth I never knew… Twenty-five years and you still ain’t clear; we fight to remember, fight through the fear. \[Outro – Spoken/Faded Ad-lib\] “I know I’m not alone… let this version stay—even if it’s just fog.” Lead: “At least this memory don’t run… ’til the morning comes.” (Ad-lib: “Hold on… through the fog”)11mo

deep (Remix)Lyrics: \[\*\*Intro – Vocals: Low, contemplative, Shimmering synth pad swells, Deep 808 pulse enters softly, Vocal glitch/stutter on 'deep' \*\*\] How deep... is your love? (Mmm, yeah) Tell me, is your love... How deep... is your love? (Just gotta know) How deep... \[Verse 1 – Vocals: Polished lead, Minimalist acoustic guitar, Intricate hi-hats begin\] See your glow in the morning feed (Scrolling through) Feel your touch, even miles between (On the screen) And the moment you go offline on me I need to feel you in my space again \[\*\*Chorus 1 – Vocals: Expansive, lush layered harmonies, Punchy 808s, Full electronic percussion, Ethereal synth arpeggios, Chorus melody feels instantly iconic, like a viral sound \*\*\] 'Cause you float to me on a quiet breeze (So easy) Keep me warm in your truth, then you subtly leave And it's my soul you need to show... How deep is your love? (Is it real?) \[Verse 2 – Vocals: Intimate, slightly processed, Subtle vocal stutter effect, Evolving pad textures\] I feel your energy, morning glow (That resonance) I hear your echo when the city's low (In my head) And the moment that you disconnect from me I just need to feel your gravity again \[\*\*Chorus 2 – Vocals: More powerful, even wider harmonies, Driving 808s, Rhythmic glitches accent, Anthemic feel, with a subtle vocal drop on "love" \*\*\] 'Cause you float to me on a quiet breeze (So easy) Keep me warm in your truth, then you subtly leave And it's my soul you need to show... How deep is your love? (Really?) \[\*\*Bridge – Vocals: Emotional swell, Deconstructed vocal harmony layers, Atmospheric guitar swells, Build tension, Lyrical shift to direct, vulnerable questioning \*\*\] And when you find me in that open space (Just us two) Keep me close to your heart, leave no trace (Of the doubt) 'Cause it's my heart you need to know... How deep is your love? (Show me now) \[\*\*Outro – Vocals: Fading, reverbed echoes, Synth pad fades slowly, 808 resonates, subtle vinyl static/digital artifact fades out, repeating "how deep" \*\*\] How deep... is your love? (The real deep) I gotta know... you gotta show me... How deep... is your love? (Still searching...)11mo

Skeet 1.3 5050\[Intro: Mo/$ DJ drops, crowd noise, filtered organ; Magz enters with cypher swagger, battle MC’s timing, ready to flip from spoken to melodic. Let every drop and shout have a trailer-pop wink.\] "Yo, it’s DJ Mo Money, Mo/$ on the decks!" (DJ drop) "Country girl meets Mo City trap beat kings—right here, right now!" (DJ drop) "We LIVE at Mo Money Studios—twenty twenty-five, let’s go, bitches!" (DJ drop) "Saddle dust on these city streets" (Crowd: Cheers, off-mic laughs) "Watch me shine, watch me eat" (Yeah) "Who said a girl can’t run this beat" (Real hot girl shit) "Saddle up, let's ride" (Giddy up) "This beat’s got the city on fire" (Yeehaw, let’s get it) "Ah-huh" (Let’s go) "Boots up!" (Now hush—let it ride) "Yeah, yeah, let's go" \[Verse 1: Use rapid-fire, internal rhymes and scientific multisyllabic phrasing; each line is bold but never loses the trailer pop melody. Lean into Eminem/Kendrick-style pocket flips, with a laugh or sneer where it fits.\] "Big buckle on my waist, neon on my name" (Whoop) "Boots so loud, they got cows feelin’ shame" (Laughter) "Mama said don’t chase those cowboy games" (Quick inhale before next bar) "But I turn that lasso into diamond chains" "He slide in my DMs talkin’ queen of the hay" "I ghost him quicker than I cash my pay" "Bass in the barn, that crowd on mute" "Boots on the porch, just me and my truth" "Country heart, city wit—can’t clone this blend" "I’m that wild-card girl, flexin’ 'til the end" \[Chorus: Hooks are melodic, anthem-ready, but cut through with battle-rap confidence and trailer-park swagger. Ad-libs should have a gospel or crowd chant bounce, with “white girl math” punchline attitude.\] "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Who’s got the boots to ball" (Crowd: "We do!") "Thick like syrup, I stick on the drawl" "Raise your cup if you heard this y’all" (Let’s go!) "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Heads turn, let ‘em fall in line" "Spin that bag, I don’t need his co-sign" "Wave your hats, let the spotlight shine" (Mis-timed clap, quick laugh left in) \[Verse 2: Drop a Boosie/Pimp C trill flex—confessional and punchy, weaving multis, trailer wisdom, and country references. Allow for micro-story and a joke or two.\] "Moonshine sippin’ out a Yeti with gold" (Off-mic whistle) "Grandpa’s truck, still ain’t been sold" "They wanna wife me for the farm and the land" "But I’m buyin’ out deeds, got my own brand" "Mama warned don’t trust his rodeo smile" "But I walked in the ring, made the judges wild" "Hat tip, crowd flip, I bend that scene" "Bass knock, boots drop, I’m the real country queen" (Voice cracks on "promo," keep it) "Farm girls mad, that’s free promo" "Catch me dancin’ in the city solo" \[Bridge: Acapella, half-spoken, Kendrick-style confession—channel the vulnerability of battle defeat and the bravado of comeback. Keep the phrasing loose, leave in the breaths, and let gospel hums echo in the background.\] "Heard girl, you can’t—since age thirteen" (Breath, near whisper) "Now I’m headline news in these boots money green" "Tried to box me in—no roof, no wall" "Country flex—watch me, no filter at all" "Phone blowin’ up, county boys in a trance" "But I’m just out here givin’ every girl a chance" (Shaky sigh, tape wobble) \[Chorus (Final): Anthem dialed to max, gospel choir behind, Magz throws in extra rhyme flips and closes with a battle-winner’s wink. Let crowd ad-libs run wild.\] "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Who’s got the boots to ball" (Let’s go) "From hayloft to high-rise, watch me run it all" "Thick as trouble, sweet as the county drawl" "Country booty call" (Crowd, wave them hats, let the barn lights fall) "I’m the headline, read it on the wall" (Late cheer, stray harmony on "call") "Boss talk, one glance—y’all know who to call" \[Outro: Band drops out, acapella with gospel melisma; Magz riffs, lets a laugh or voice crack land, closes with Mo/$ DJ drop. Let the last line hang, full of attitude and promise.\] "Kick dust, blow a kiss, tip the brim" (Boots up!) "Who’s the queen, say my name again" (Country girl signed out) "Bass fades, I wink, camera flash" "Roll out solo, let the rumors dash" "Now watch ‘em all try to copy the route" (Mo/$: "Magnolia Magz, Mo Money Studios, twenty twenty-five!")1y

Amazing Grace (radio)\[Theory\] \[mode | D major with gospel IV-modal shifts\] \[tonal center | D\] \[meter | 4/4 shuffled swing\] \[tempo | 70 BPM trap-slow bounce\] \[chord color | gospel suspensions, blues grace tones, IV lifts\] \[Voice\] \[register | low tenor with worn texture and dry presence\] \[delivery | preacher-style phrasing with staggered space for testimony\] \[expression | reverent and raw, survivor-sung from memory not myth\] \[Style\] \[genre | Gospel-Trap Americana Revival\] \[era | post-2025 analog tape soul\] \[intent | sacred story told through lived struggle and true grace\] \[texture | upright bass, Hammond B3, analog stomp-kit, slide guitar, sub-layer\] \[aesthetic | small church fire meets slow-roll slab trunk honesty\] \[focus | original lyrics, phrased bar-for-bar with gospel energy\] \[Timbre\] \[drum tone | brushed snare, rim tap, loose hi-hat swing\] \[bass tone | upright body + warm sub layer\] \[keyboard tone | Hammond B3 with analog flutter\] \[guitar tone | muted slide + tape delay\] \[fx palette | tape hiss, vinyl crackle, low-end reverb bloom\] \[vocal tone | dry mic + soft plate on choir, breaths intact\] \[Performance\] "Child, don’t stray." "But I preach pain... ‘till bills get paid." "Bent but breathin’... eyes on grace." "Let strangers touch... what God never meant." "My name ain’t shame... it's in gold." "In fire... and sweat... my story told." — \[vocalist – MALE SHADOW + FEMALE SHOUT | reverb swell –\] "She a prophet... in pole-light." "I ain’t lost... I’m in plain sight." "I rise from pain... with every plea." "I sip... I spin... and still I’m free." — \[vocalist – FEMALE CHOIR STACK | tape echo, adlib: “Hallelujah” –\] "Jus’ you & me... no veil... no shame." "This pain got rhythm... this stage my name." "He lied... but I see... and I believe." "I dance... I fall... but I still breathe." — \[vocalist – MALE & FEMALE HARMONY WHISPER | vinyl fade –\] "So I spin... and I sip..." "But the Lord... don’t slip..." Country Booty Call BOOM: tna\[DJ Drop: Mo/$ DJ drops, crowd noise, filtered organ; Magz enters with cypher swagger, battle MC’s timing, ready to flip from spoken to melodic. Let every drop and shout have a trailer-pop wink.\] "Yo, it’s DJ Mo Money, Mo/$ on the decks!" (DJ drop) "Country girl meets Mo City trap beat kings—right here, right now!" (DJ drop) "We LYV at Mo Money Studios—twenty twenty-five, let’s go, bitches!" (DJ drop) \[Intro\] "Saddle dust on these city streets" (Crowd: Cheers, off-mic laughs) "Watch me shine, watch me eat" (Yeah) "Who said a girl can’t run this beat" (Real hot girl shit) "Saddle up, let's ride" (Giddy up) "This beat’s got the city on fire" (Yeehaw, let’s get it) "Ah-huh" (Let’s go) "Boots up!" (Now hush—let it ride) "Yeah, yeah, let's go" \[Verse 1: Use rapid-fire, internal rhymes and scientific multisyllabic phrasing; each line is bold but never loses the trailer pop melody. Lean into Eminem/Kendrick-style pocket flips, with a laugh or sneer where it fits.\] "Big buckle on my waist, neon on my name" (Whoop) "Boots so loud, they got cows feelin’ shame" (Laughter) "Mama said don’t chase those cowboy games" (Quick inhale before next bar) "But I turn that lasso into diamond chains" "He slide in my DMs talkin’ queen of the hay" "I ghost him quicker than I cash my pay" "Bass in the barn, that crowd on mute" "Boots on the porch, just me and my truth" "Country heart, city wit—can’t clone this blend" "I’m that wild-card girl, flexin’ 'til the end" \[Chorus: Hooks are melodic, anthem-ready, but cut through with battle-rap confidence and trailer-park swagger. Ad-libs should have a gospel or crowd chant bounce, with “white girl math” punchline attitude.\] "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Who’s got the boots to ball" (Crowd: "We do!") "Thick like syrup, I stick on the drawl" "Raise your cup if you heard this y’all" (Let’s go!) "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Heads turn, let ‘em fall in line" "Spin that bag, I don’t need his co-sign" "Wave your hats, let the spotlight shine" (Mis-timed clap, quick laugh left in) \[Verse 2: Drop a Boosie/Pimp C trill flex—confessional and punchy, weaving multis, trailer wisdom, and country references. Allow for micro-story and a joke or two.\] "Moonshine sippin’ out a Yeti with gold" (Off-mic whistle) "Grandpa’s truck, still ain’t been sold" "They wanna wife me for the farm and the land" "But I’m buyin’ out deeds, got my own brand" "Mama warned don’t trust his rodeo smile" "But I walked in the ring, made the judges wild" "Hat tip, crowd flip, I bend that scene" "Bass knock, boots drop, I’m the real country queen" (Voice cracks on "promo," keep it) "Farm girls mad, that’s free promo" "Catch me dancin’ in the city solo" \[Bridge: Acapella, half-spoken, Kendrick-style confession—channel the vulnerability of battle defeat and the bravado of comeback. Keep the phrasing loose, leave in the breaths, and let gospel hums echo in the background.\] "Heard girl, you can’t—since age thirteen" (Breath, near whisper) "Now I’m headline news in these boots money green" "Tried to box me in—no roof, no wall" "Country flex—watch me, no filter at all" "Phone blowin’ up, county boys in a trance" "But I’m just out here givin’ every girl a chance" (Shaky sigh, tape wobble) \[Chorus (Final): Anthem dialed to max, gospel choir behind, Magz throws in extra rhyme flips and closes with a battle-winner’s wink. Let crowd ad-libs run wild.\] "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Who’s got the boots to ball" (Let’s go) "From hayloft to high-rise, watch me run it all" "Thick as trouble, sweet as the county drawl" "Country booty call" (Crowd, wave them hats, let the barn lights fall) "I’m the headline, read it on the wall" (Late cheer, stray harmony on "call") "Boss talk, one glance—y’all know who to call" \[Outro: Band drops out, acapella with gospel melisma; Magz riffs, lets a laugh or voice crack land, closes with Mo/$ DJ drop. Let the last line hang, full of attitude and promise.\] "Kick dust, blow a kiss, tip the brim" (Boots up!) "Who’s the queen, say my name again" (Country girl signed out) "Bass fades, I wink, camera flash" "Roll out solo, let the rumors dash" "Now watch ‘em all try to copy the route" (Mo/$: "Magnolia Magz, Mo Money Studios, twenty twenty-five!")1y

Just You and Me v2 80-75-50\[Theory\] \[mode | Aeolian (natural minor)\] \[tonal center | A\] \[meter | 4/4\] \[tempo | 72 BPM slow, head-nodding\] \[chord color | minor iv–VI progressions with honky-tonk embellishments\] \[Voice\] \[register | female alto/mezzo-soprano\] \[delivery | deep, smoky, breathy storytelling\] \[expression | gritty, vulnerable\] \[articulation | legato lines with whispered rasp and subtle rasp\] \[Style\] \[genre | Country Trap · O.G. Boom Bap · Southern Soul-Zydeco fusion\] \[era | 2020s boom-bap warmth meets neon barroom grit\] \[intent | raw storytelling of a dancer’s struggle and search for salvation\] \[texture | syncopated trap beats · twangy guitar · honky-tonk piano · gospel background harmonies\] \[aesthetic | neon-soaked bar confessional\] \[focus | narrative authenticity and emotional delivery\] \[Timbre\] \[drum tone | heavy 808 mid-bass punch with UK-drill hi-hat swirl\] \[bass tone | rolling sub-bass with mid-bass stutter\] \[keyboard tone | honky-tonk piano with smoky organ underscoring\] \[guitar tone | sparse slide and twang guitar moans\] \[fx palette | vinyl crackle · distant bar chatter · slide guitar moans\] \[vocal tone | deep, smoky lead with warm gospel-style reverb\] \[Performance\] \[execution | Intro → Verse 1 → Chorus → Verse 2 → Bridge → Chorus Reprise → Outro\] \[gesture | whispered cough cuts · slide-guitar moans · beat lags like a heartbeat\] \[rhythm handling | nonlinear beat-grid with stuttering 808s and drill-style hi-hats\] \[touch | raw ad-libs · glitchy drag-out ending\] \[CREW\_TAGS - Alt tags (“Ooooh” · “have mercy” · “jus’ you & me” )\] \[Road-Map: 0:00-0:15 Intro – whispered grit, distant bar sounds, hollow bass, slide guitar 0:15-0:45 Verse 1 – sparse kick, heavy boom-bap 808s, slow twang guitar, raw storytelling 0:45-1:15 Chorus – gospel background harmonies, honky-tonk piano, boom-bap bounce 1:15-1:45 Verse 2 – twangy guitar meets boom-bap, breathless delivery 1:45-2:15 Bridge – a cappella gospel with sub-bass pulse, melodic percussion 2:15-2:45 Chorus Reprise – full layers, gritty vocal belt, glitch drag tension 2:45-3:00 Outro – slide guitar bends, bar sounds, vinyl crackle fade\] ▸ LYRICS BLOCK \[Intro: Distant Bar Sounds, Hollow Bass, Slide Guitar\] \[Female Lead, whispered with grit\] "Neon hums, last call echoes... Smoke curls thick, my sins still show... Ooooh, jus’ you & me..." (\*A cough cuts through. Slide guitar moans low. Kick drum lags like a heartbeat on edge.\*) \[Verse 1: Sparse Kick, Heavy Boom Bap 808s, Slow Twang Guitar\] \[Female Lead, low & smoky\] "He slid a twenty cross the stage last night, Said, ‘Dance, baby, dance,’ like he owned my fight. Mama left when I was just a kid, Neon raised me where the whiskey slid." \[Mid-bass 808s stutter, UK Drill-style hi-hats swirl, layering the groove.\] "I grip that pole like a prayer gone cold, Spin through smoke, let my pain unfold. Every song’s the same, every hand still takes, But this bottle don’t judge my breaks." \[Chorus: Gospel Harmonies (Background Only), Boom Bap Bounce, Honky-Tonk Piano\] \[Female Lead, deep and powerful\] "Jus’ you & me, on this hardwood stage, Dollar bills fall, but they don’t buy change. Whiskey talks sweet, but it don’t set me free, Still I sip, still I spin—Lord, just let me be." \[Sub-bass 808s roll slow, steel guitar wails faintly in the back.\] \[Verse 2: Twangy Guitar, Boom Bap Meets Country, Raw Delivery\] \[Female Lead, breathless & heavy\] "Smoke swirls thick where the drunk men stare, Their rings still on, but they don’t care. Granny’s hymn cuts through my haze, ‘Lawd, child, don’t you lose your ways.’" \[Heavy 808s thud like boots stomping on wood; the nonlinear beat grid keeps the groove unpredictable.\] "Bent back, eyes shut, red lights blur, I fake a smile, but the world still stirs. Grippin’ the pole, same hands they crave, Lord, am I saved, or just too far away?" \[Bridge: A Cappella Gospel with Sub-Bass Pulse, Melodic Percussion\] \[Female Lead, hushed & vulnerable\] "Granny’s voice keeps callin’ me home, Through sins and smoke where the lost still roam. A light shines bright, it won’t let me go— A hymn of hope from so long ago." \[Then—BOOM—heavy 808s and melodic percussion drop back in with UK Drill syncopation.\] \[Chorus Reprise: Gospel Swells, Heavy 808s (All Layers), Gritty Vocal Belt\] \[Female Lead, belting raw emotion\] "Jus’ you & me, on this hardwood stage, Dollar bills fall, but they don’t buy change. Whiskey talks sweet, but it don’t set me free, Still I sip, still I spin—Lord, just let me be." \[The beat glitches, dragging out tension before stopping—leaving just her voice, cracked and breathless.\] \[Outro: Slide Guitar Bends, Bar Sounds, Vinyl Crackle\] \[Female Lead, whispered, confessional\] "Ooooh… have mercy on me… It’s jus’ you & me." \[A lone steel guitar weeps, blending into the faint sounds of a hushed crowd that then EXPLODES IN APPLAUSE!!!!\]1y

I said, 'Never'" "And I put it in my verse, she think she so clever" "And she used to love me 'cause I do it better" "Better, better, better, better, better, better, better" (Auto-panned L–R, vocoder FX, delay trail on final “better”) \[Chorus – Chant-Style Hook, Stacked Vocals, Ambient Reverb Pad\] "Ayy, they said it couldn't be done, it's just another rerun" (Reverb swell) "Just give it to me, like, run it to me" (Wide pan, autotuned) "They said it couldn't be done, it's just another rerun" "Just give it to me, like, run it to me" (Last “run” pitched up) \[Post-Chorus – Mantra Loop w/ FX Variation\] "Run it to me" (Dry) "Run it to me" (Stereo + slap delay) "Run it to me" (Pitched + distant) "Run it to me" (Vocoder) \[Verse 2 – Distorted Double Layer, Lo-Fi Section at “Mental” Bar\] "Fifteen years, and I came back, like, 'Hey, yo'" "Takin' niggas' heads off, that's fatal" "Now it's fuck you, pay me, then I lay low" "In my head, I know this shit is all mental" (Lowpass filter drop) "It's the family over everything, so I treat it like a bando" "Baby wanna know what my plans for today" "Is you with me? Is you not? Is you in? Is you out?" "I can still tell that you're not all the way convinced" "But my actions, I won't try to convince" "Take you to the land, like, when is you gonna come?" (Echo delay) "Would you hold the line, or just play for free?" "Got a pocket full of love, but the price ain’t cheap" "So baby, if you want it, gotta run it to me" \[Final Chorus – Chopped Vocal FX Underneath\] "Ayy, they said it couldn't be done, it's just another rerun" "Just give it to me, like, run it to me" "They said it couldn't be done, it's just another rerun" "Just give it to me, like, run it to me" \[Outro – Tape Hiss, Chopped + Pitched “Run It To Me”\] "Run it to me..." "Run it to me..." (Slowdown) "Run it..." This Love Is Dangerous (Remix)Your nails down my back like a tattoo of sin, I know I should run—but I keep comin back in. You taste like temptation, laced with regret, But the thought of you… and I’m holdin’ my breath. We both know this love’s a slow bleed, But your body talkin’ like it’s just what I need… \[Pre-Chorus\] I should leave at sunrise… (But your legs got me prayin’ for the night.) You should hate my lies… (But you love how they whisper when I’m inside.) \[Chorus\] This love is dangerous, baby, You hold onto fears just to lay down and crave me. Seeking relief in …a bed full of toxins, We should stop… but we won’t— ‘Cause the poison taste sweet when it’s warmed \[Verse 2\] You tell me this is a first, I tell you you are my best, We kiss like truth, but we both know the rest, Your moans sound honest, my hands still confess, Two liars in love, both failing the test. You deserve angel love— But you keep fallin’ for the devil’s touch. \[Bridge\] "Tell me you hate me… (While your lips savor my name.) Tell me you’ll leave me … (While your hips beg me to stay.)" \[Chorus\] (Repeat – more intense) "This love is dangerous, baby, The way you let me ruin you so sweetly. I’m no good, but you love me the hardest, Fingers in my hair while I’m tearin’ your heart out. We should stop… but we won’t— ‘Cause the pain feels like love when it’s raw." \[Outro\] (Fading into the night) "Dangerous love… We’ll never get enough… Dangerous love… God damn us."1y

I came through clean, linen drippin’ like rain Roses in my ride, body still smellin’ like fame I parked three houses down like I always do Waited on her man to leave — that’s my cue He did his lil’ routine, kissed her like a show Backed out slow, she waved... I thought I know Then a Benz I ain’t seen before Pulled up slick with suicide doors She ran to him like I was never in her plans I dropped my flowers like a fool with empty hands \[Hook – Talkbox + Johnny Lead Harmony\] She’s cheatin’ on us... cheatin’ on trust... Playin’ two fools like a playlist dusted up I was her weekend, you was her man But now we both on read, left on her OnlyFans (Talkbox harmonizes “OnlyFaaanssss…”) \[Verse 2 – Grownman Breakdown Flow + Soul Croon\] She told me you was cold Told you I was bold Told him he was old Told all of us lies in gold I was just the thrill — you the bill Now she backseat ridin’ like she never will I loved her in cashapp confessions Took her to courtrooms and confessions I prayed for her while she textin’ Another man with no discretion \[Bridge – Funk Talk, Swung Hi-Hat Groove\] “It ain’t no competition when everybody losin’.” “You think you exclusive... But she treatin’ hearts like p. diddy.... abusive.” (FX: Auto-tuned sigh, organ swirl) \[Breakdown – Strip it to Moog + Reverb\] She’s cheatin’ on us (repeat 2x) And I still miss her touch She’s cheatin’ on us (repeat 2x) But I still might pull up (slow bend guitar lick echoes like a drunk voicemail) \[Outro – Trap Blues Falsetto w/ Screwed Adlibs\] I ain’t your enemy, I’m your echo... We both loved a hologram in stilettos... She used to text "I love you" But that was a group text, bro… (FX: Talkbox “Damn.” + voicemail beep)1y

Country Booty Call - DJ MoMoney xs (Remix) SDSD (Remix)\[DJ Drop: Mo/$ DJ drops, chopped and screw and scratches introduction with crowd noise, filtered organ; Magz enters with cypher swagger, battle MC’s timing, ready to flip from spoken to melodic. (DJ drop) "We LIVE at Mo Money Studios—twenty twenty-five, let’s go, bitches!" (DJ drop) \[INTRO - Advanced turntablism with scratches while putting other djs and producers on notice as i chop and screww the whole song) "Saddle dust on these city streets" (Crowd: Cheers, off-mic laughs) "Watch me shine, watch me eat" (Yeah) "Who said a girl can’t run this beat" (Real hot girl shit) "Saddle up, let's ride" (Giddy up) "This beat’s got the city on fire" (Yeehaw, let’s get it) "Ah-huh" (Let’s go) "Boots up!" (Now hush—let it ride) "Yeah, yeah, let's go" \[Verse 1: Use rapid-fire, internal rhymes and scientific multisyllabic phrasing; each line is bold but never loses the trailer pop melody. Lean into Eminem/Kendrick-style pocket flips, with a laugh or sneer where it fits.\] "Big buckle on my waist, neon on my name" (Whoop) "Boots so loud, they got cows feelin’ shame" (Laughter) "Mama said don’t chase those cowboy games" (Quick inhale before next bar) "But I turn that lasso into diamond chains" "He slide in my DMs talkin’ queen of the hay" "I ghost him quicker than I cash my pay" "Bass in the barn, that crowd on mute" "Boots on the porch, just me and my truth" "Country heart, city wit—can’t clone this blend" "I’m that wild-card girl, flexin’ 'til the end" \[Chorus: Hooks are melodic, anthem-ready, but cut through with battle-rap confidence and trailer-park swagger. Ad-libs should have a gospel or crowd chant bounce, with “white girl math” punchline attitude.\] "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Who’s got the boots to ball" (Crowd: "We do!") "Thick like syrup, I stick on the drawl" "Raise your cup if you heard this y’all" (Let’s go!) "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Heads turn, let ‘em fall in line" "Spin that bag, I don’t need his co-sign" "Wave your hats, let the spotlight shine" (Mis-timed clap, quick laugh left in) \[Verse 2: Drop a Boosie/Pimp C trill flex—confessional and punchy, weaving multis, trailer wisdom, and country references. Allow for micro-story and a joke or two.\] "Moonshine sippin’ out a Yeti with gold" (Off-mic whistle) "Grandpa’s truck, still ain’t been sold" "They wanna wife me for the farm and the land" "But I’m buyin’ out deeds, got my own brand" "Mama warned don’t trust his rodeo smile" "But I walked in the ring, made the judges wild" "Hat tip, crowd flip, I bend that scene" "Bass knock, boots drop, I’m the real country queen" (Voice cracks on "promo," keep it) "Farm girls mad, that’s free promo" "Catch me dancin’ in the city solo" \[Bridge: Acapella, half-spoken, Kendrick-style confession—channel the vulnerability of battle defeat and the bravado of comeback. Keep the phrasing loose, leave in the breaths, and let gospel hums echo in the background.\] "Heard girl, you can’t—since age thirteen" (Breath, near whisper) "Now I’m headline news in these boots money green" "Tried to box me in—no roof, no wall" "Country flex—watch me, no filter at all" "Phone blowin’ up, county boys in a trance" "But I’m just out here givin’ every girl a chance" (Shaky sigh, tape wobble) \[Chorus (Final): Anthem dialed to max, gospel choir behind, Magz throws in extra rhyme flips and closes with a battle-winner’s wink. Let crowd ad-libs run wild.\] "Country booty call" (Crowd: "Booty call!") "Who’s got the boots to ball" (Let’s go) "From hayloft to high-rise, watch me run it all" "Thick as trouble, sweet as the county drawl" "Country booty call" (Crowd, wave them hats, let the barn lights fall) "I’m the headline, read it on the wall" (Late cheer, stray harmony on "call") "Boss talk, one glance—y’all know who to call" \[Outro: Band drops out, acapella with gospel melisma; Magz riffs, lets a laugh or voice crack land, closes with Mo/$ DJ drop. Let the last line hang, full of attitude and promise.\] "Kick dust, blow a kiss, tip the brim" (Boots up!) "Who’s the queen, say my name again" (Country girl signed out) "Bass fades, I wink, camera flash" "Roll out solo, let the rumors dash" "Now watch ‘em all try to copy the route" (Mo/$: "Magnolia Magz, Mo Money Studios, twenty twenty-five!")1y

Thick like syrup, I stick on the drawl Raise your cup if you heard this y’all (Let’s go!) Country booty call— Heads turn, let ‘em fall in line Spin that bag, I don’t need no sign Wave your hats, let the spotlight shine! \[Verse 2 – Internal rhymes, story twist, wit, swing\] Moonshine sippin’ out a Yeti with gold Grandpa’s truck, still ain’t been sold They wanna wife me for the farm and the land But I’m buyin’ out deeds, got my own brand Mama warned: “Don’t trust that rodeo smile” But I walked in the ring, made the judges wild Hat tip, crowd flip, I bend that scene Bass knock, boots drop, I’m country queen Farm girls mad? That’s free promo Catch me dancin’ in the city—solo \[Bridge – Micro-story, self-aware, softer note\] Heard “girl, you can’t”—since age thirteen Now I’m headline news in these boots of green Tried to box me in—no roof, no wall Country flex—watch me, no filter at all Phone blowin’ up, county boys in a trance But I’m just out here—givin’ every girl a chance \[Chorus – Flipped for final crowd chant, extra chant line\] Country booty call— Who’s got the boots to ball? (Let’s go!) From hayloft to high-rise, watch me run it all Thick as trouble, sweet as the county drawl Country booty call— Crowd, wave them hats, let the barn lights fall I’m the headline—read it on the wall Boss talk, one glance—y’all know who to call \[Outro – Memorable, meme-able, camera-facing\] Kick dust, blow a kiss, tip the brim Who’s the queen? Say my name again Bass fades, I wink, camera flash— Roll out solo, let the rumors dash (Boots up!) Country girl signed out— Now watch ‘em all try to copy the route.1y

The Soul Sessions: Getaway (Until Sunday)\[Intro – Lo-Fi Static, Faint Heartbeat\] (Husband’s voice, weary, whispered) I swear to God we were just friends... (Static crackles, a slow, heavy heartbeat beneath) Suddenly... we were both lonely. You didn’t even notice... I’d started drinking again. ‘Cause I was lonely... and you just ignore... and hate all of my friends. You stopped looking at me. I became a ghost in our own home. \[Verse 1 – Melancholic, Storytelling\] So I was at the bar... drinking alone. (Glasses clinking faintly, murmurs, the sound of a drink being poured) She slid beside me... I thought I’d found a moment’s peace. A smile in the smoke, a kindness I hadn’t seen in weeks. But I swear to God, I didn’t mean to cross that line. A minute turned an hour... an hour felt like a sign. And her laughter, sharp like glass, cut through the fog. \[Pre-Chorus – Suspenseful, Whispered Echoes\] And your silence screams... ‘getaway’... cuts me to the bone. I felt it every time I walked through the door... cold like stone. Getaway... leave today... stay away... (Echoes, fading like a ghost whisper) \[Verse 2 – The Bar Scene, Her Discovery\] (Sounds of a door slamming open) And then she walked in... rage like a storm, eyes wild. How could you... why would... who is she? GETAWAY... LEAVE TODAY... STAY AWAY... (Distorted, overlapping, her voice cracking) Her breath like fire, her fists like thunder. \[Chorus – Dramatic, Emotional Explosion\] And I said... I’m sorry babe... I lost your trust today. I swear, I’ll do anything... please... just don’t turn away. I never meant for the ice between us... but I see it now. \[Bridge – Minimal, Desperate Tone\] (Husband’s voice, wavering, raw) And she said... I’m sorry, I didn’t realize... I WASN’T THERE FOR YOU, AND WE BEEN TOGETHER TOO LONG... TO LET THIS MARRIAGE END. BUT FIRST... WE NEED TO WALK IN EACH OTHER'S SHOES... JUST SO YOU UNDERSTAND... so I need to meet her husband. \[Chorus Reprise – Cold, Calculating\] And I asked WHY? (Her voice, eerily calm, each word a knife) I’m feeling lonely, I can’t ignore this. I refuse to let you two win. Imma be at her house... with her husband. After we spend the night in our bed. \[Outro – Sparse, Vinyl Crackle, Looming Dread\] (Hollow, the room feels empty) So while I get ready... I’m going to need you to... GETAWAY... LEAVE TODAY... STAY AWAY... until Sunday afternoon. (Heartbeat slows, crackle deepens, fades into silence)1y

Tumbleweed spin down a one-lane track, (Cover)\[Verse 1 Female Vocal – Southern drawl, pain-soaked, church-raised, microtonal singing, vocal fry, delayed delivery\] Tumbleweed spin down a one-lane track, Moonlight drip like bourbon through a broken crack. (Whoo...) – \[vocal fry adlib, offbeat echo\] (Lawd, have mercy…) – \[spoken, low, cracked tone\] \[Verse 3, slide + shamisen trade licks, breath between bars\] He sit in shadow, brim pulled down, Scars like stories—ain’t no words around. “Tell me,” he drawls, “what weight you hold?” She laugh like glass: “More than the devil been told.” \[Verse 4, thunder FX rise, ambient rain, bass drag\] Thunder crack, sky cry loud, Dust turn to mud where pain allowed. She pull her collar, he reach that hand— Some roads don’t walk with just one man. \[Chorus 2, vocal stack, whistle harmony, emotional stretch\] Whiskey and wild roses—wild but true, Fire kissin’ water, baptized in blue. Through storm and shadow, side by side, Whiskey and wild roses—no place to hide. oh death angry (Cover)\[Production Notes: This version opens with angry female spoken word over dry, muted kick — no melody, just breath and bitterness. As the verse unfolds, a raw Southern Black choir enters with disharmonized minor chord echoes. Snare arrives like a heartbeat breaking free. Instruments only enter as accents — organ drone, sub bass, chopped fx appear only after vocal climax. Emotion > Perfection. Tension is the glue.\] \[Intro – Spoken Word, Dry Kick Only\] (dry muted kick: 4-count loop) Lead (sharp, pissed): "I ain’t scared of you. You walk like a king, but you creep like a coward. Say my name all low — say it loud. DEATH. You can’t have me." (pause. breath. inhale like thunder.) "Not today." \[Verse 1 – Spoken-Sing Hybrid, Dry Kick + Snare Enters Slowly\] "I felt you behind me — Boots in my kitchen, breath on my bed. You think I ain't seen you? You BEEN in my head." "Mama said light a candle. Daddy said pour a drink. I just closed my eyes and prayed that I don’t overthink." (snare hits once — ghost echo trail) "You don’t knock loud — You just stand there. But I hear you anyway. You want me scared?" \[Choir Enters – Minor Harmony Echoes, Imperfect and Raw\] \*(Choir hum enters in minor; not tight, just thick) Choir (response, low): “Not today…” Lead (sharp): “I SAID NOT TODAY.” Choir (rising): “You can’t have her…” Lead (building): “YOU DON’T OWN THIS BREATH.” \[Bridge – Beat Build, Organ Enters, Choir Swells\] (organ enters under, low and dirty) (snare now steady, kick thickens) Lead: "I still got breath. I still got fight. You circle me daily, But you won’t win tonight." (Choir builds into a wall — wailing minor chords over lead’s major scale phrasing) \[Final Chorus – Full Layer, Tension Peaking\] Lead (full belt): "O DEATH — I WON’T KNEEL! I still breathe DEEP! My soul ain’t clean — But it ain’t YOURS to KEEP!" Choir (off-key echo, swelling): “Not yours… not yours… not yours…” (sub bass rumbles under the choir. final organ chord holds.) \[Outro – Fade on Breath + Organ Ring\] Lead (half-whispered): "You didn’t write my name. So you don’t get to end it." \*(end with ambient trail, chopped final whisper: “Earn… your… name…")\* --- \*\*Emotion Arc (Mapped Per Section):\*\* - \*\*Intro → Verse 1:\*\* Seductive + strategic entry, establishing power through presence - \*\*Chorus 1:\*\* Declarative ownership, club dominance, poetic threat - \*\*Verse 2:\*\* Strategic tension rises, dominance coded in economic language - \*\*Chorus 2:\*\* Repetition intensifies, layered with legacy callouts - \*\*Outro:\*\* Withdrawal, ghosting, metaphysical departure — emotional vacuum left behind1y
